newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT BACKS SAVINGS BANK CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT BACKS SAVINGS BANK CAPITAL.

text.p: The Lithuanian government on Wednesday backed a proposal to increase the share capital of state-owned Savings Bank by 20 million litas.

The government press office said in a statement that the cabinet approved a proposal from the finance ministry, which controls the state's share in the bank, to vote for the share capital rise at a shareholder meeting on Friday.
The cabinet also approved a change in the nominal value of Savings Bank shares to split every 100 litas face value share to 10 shares with one litas face value.
Some six million litas of the capital rise will come from own reserves and 14 million litas from additional contributions. The capital will rise to 80 million litas after the increase.
The state owns 74 percent of the bank and the rest is in private hands.
It is the only state-run bank of three that has not been slated for privatisation.
The state will be represented by four board members on the bank's council.
